papers_read.title_as_printed: Machine learning of brain structural biomarkers for Alzheimer's disease (AD) diagnosis, prediction of disease progression, and amyloid beta deposition in the Japanese population (Shiino et al., Alzheimer's Dement DADM 2021)
A dynamic time series inference learning framework for individualized prediction of mild cognitive impairment progression (Xu et al., Expert Syst Appl 2026)

what_each_reports.P-187: BAAD VBM-ROI SVM trained and tuned on North American ADNI, applied to 1.5T baseline MRI of the Japanese ADNI (J-ADNI). Prediction of disease progression in NON-DEMENTIA participants (387 NL or MCI; 119 MCI->AD, 4 NL->MCI, 1 NL->AD over 3 years): accuracy 77.4-79.4% for ADLS and 79.6-80.4% for ADLSc (MRI+MMSE); abstract gives 76.0-79.3%. No AUC for progression in the main text.
what_each_reports.P-78: Longitudinal sMRI 3D-DenseNet + Transformer (DTI/DDAS/JTOS) trained on ADNI-1/2/GO. The 90.7% accuracy (AUC 0.871) is the four-time-point (QTP) ablation on Dataset B (101 held-out ADNI-1/2/GO MCI subjects, 36-month window). Single-time-point (STP) on the same Dataset B: ACC 0.763 (95% CI 0.711-0.816), AUC 0.832. External Dataset A (ADNI-3 + OASIS-3 baseline): ACC 0.827, AUC 0.858.

quantity_a: Accuracy of a single baseline MRI-derived AD-likelihood score for 3-year progression among Japanese non-demented participants (NL and MCI pooled; progression includes NL->MCI), model trained on a different cohort (North American ADNI).
quantity_b: Accuracy of a model using four longitudinal sMRI scans over 36 months to classify pMCI vs sMCI among 101 held-out ADNI-1/2/GO MCI subjects (internal held-out split).
incompatible_if_same: No. At the nearest matched quantity (single baseline scan), P-78's STP accuracy is 0.763 with 95% CI 0.711-0.816, which contains P-187's 77.4-79.4%; the recorded 90.7% exists only with four scans.

gates.task: partial: both 3-year progression prediction, but P-187's population includes normal controls (NL->MCI counted as progression) while P-78 is MCI-only pMCI vs sMCI
gates.dataset_family: mismatch: P-187 is J-ADNI (Japanese ADNI, 38 Japanese sites), a distinct cohort from North American ADNI used by P-78; the record's 'dataset_equal: Yes' is wrong
gates.validation_tier: mismatch: P-187 applies an ADNI-trained model to an independent cohort (external); P-78's 90.7% is on an internal held-out ADNI split
gates.modality_family: match: structural MRI (P-187's ADLSc variant adds MMSE)

endpoint_and_metric: incompatible: both accuracy, but input representation differs (one baseline scan vs four longitudinal scans), population differs (NL+MCI vs MCI only) and cohort differs
performance_validity: flag does not apply: both below 0.97
independence: Distinct author groups and distinct cohorts (J-ADNI vs ADNI/OASIS); P-187's model was tuned on North American ADNI, which P-78 also uses.
grounds: P-78's 90.7% accuracy is its four-time-point longitudinal result, whereas P-187 predicts from a single baseline scan, so the input representation differs.
P-187 pools normal and MCI participants in J-ADNI and counts NL->MCI as progression, whereas P-78 classifies MCI only in ADNI, so population and dataset family differ.
At the matched single-scan setting P-78 reports 76.3% (95% CI 71.1-81.6%), which contains P-187's 77.4-79.4%, so no disagreement appears where the quantities approach each other.

evidence_quotes.quote: During the 3 years of observation, among the 387 participants with NL or MCI, 119 MCI had converted to AD, 4 NL to MCI, and one NL to AD.
The prediction accuracy of disease progression in non-dementia individuals was 77.4% to 79.4% for ADLS and 79.6% to 80.4% for ADLSc.
We used the radial basis function as the kernel for the SVM, and the values of parameters were optimized using the North American ADNI database.
The model achieved peak performance with QTP, recording an AUC of 87.1 % and an ACC of 90.7 %. Compared to STP, DTP, and TTP, the ACC improved by 14.4 %, 7.7 %, and 3.8 %, respectively
Ultimately, 101 subjects who met the above longitudinal criteria were selected from a total of 486 subjects, and 304 sMRI images were obtained, forming Dataset B.

record_defects: resolution_note gives 'Task mismatch from summaries: T1_mci_vs_hc vs T2_conversion' as the reason; both papers report 3-year progression prediction, so that stated reason is wrong.
dataset_equal 'Yes' and registry Dataset 'ADNI' for P-187 are wrong: P-187 uses the Japanese ADNI (J-ADNI) with a model trained on North American ADNI.
P-187 registry Validation_Type V2 is wrong for the J-ADNI application of an ADNI-trained model (external).
claim_a 'Acc 79.3' comes from the abstract range 76.0-79.3%; the results text gives 77.4-79.4% (ADLS) and 79.6-80.4% (ADLSc).
claim_b '90.7% Acc' does not say it needs four longitudinal scans; P-78's single-scan external result is 82.7% and internal STP is 76.3%.
P-78 registry Validation_Type V4 applies to Dataset A (ADNI-3/OASIS-3, ACC 0.827), not to the 90.7% figure, which is on the internal Dataset B.
what_would_change_the_verdict: A single-baseline-scan, MCI-only, same-cohort accuracy from P-78 whose CI excluded P-187's range; the reported STP CI includes it.
